newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania poll shows slight Dole gain.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania poll shows slight Dole gain.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole gained slightly on President Clinton in a statewide poll of Pennsylvania voters released Wednesday.
Clinton led Dole 48 percent to 36 percent in the latest KYW-Philadelphia Daily News Keystone poll of 695 likely voters. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot was a distant third with 7 percent support.
Clinton's 12-point lead was down four points from a month earlier.

The narrowing margin could reduce Clinton's chances of carrying to victory Democratic candidates for Congress and state offices in next Tuesday's election, said Terry Madonna, a Millersville University political scientist and director of the poll.

"If Clinton's lead drops to, say, 10 points, there will be much less of a coattails effect, and that helps Republicans statewide and in legislative and Congressional races," the Daily News quoted Madonna as saying.
Pennsylvania, the fifth largest electoral state with 23 electoral votes of 270 needed to win the presidency, has been regarded as a key battleground state.
The poll's margin of error was 3.7 percent.
